info.name: CustomerHub ValidationServices - QA Suite
info.description:
# CustomerHub ValidationServices - QA Suite

Functional, contract, boundary, security and traceability tests for the **ValidationServices** Spring Boot API
(`/api/v1/data-quality`). Every request carries automated assertions, so the whole collection can run unattended
in the Postman Runner or in CI with Newman.

## Endpoints covered

| Endpoint | Purpose | Success status |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /validate-name` | Person name rules and normalisation | 200 valid / **422** invalid |
| `POST /validate-email` | Email syntax and denylist | 200 (see `syntaxValid`) |
| `POST /validate-phone` | NANP / international phone rules | 200 (see `syntaxValid`) |
| `POST /validate-address` | USPS / Canada Post normalisation, denylist, store crossover | 200 (see `valid`) |
| `POST /validate-profile` | Full profile decision: ACCEPT / ACCEPT_WITH_WARNINGS / REJECT | 200 (see `decision`) |
| `GET /actuator/health` | Liveness / readiness | 200 |

## Getting started

1. Import the collection and the three environment files (`Local`, `DEV`, `TEST`).
2. Select an environment and set `baseUrl` (DEV and TEST ship with a placeholder host to replace).
3. Optional: to run folder **06**, edit its request bodies so the denylist / store values exist in your
   database, then set `runReferenceDataTests` to `true`.
4. Run the collection (Runner) or a single folder. Run **00 Health** first.

## Variables

| Variable | Scope | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | environment | Service root, e.g. `http://localhost:8080` (no trailing slash) |
| `apiBasePath` | collection | `/api/v1/data-quality` |
| `slaMs` | environment | Response-time budget asserted on every request (default 2000 ms) |
| `runReferenceDataTests` | environment | `true` runs folder 06; `false` skips it (default for DEV and TEST) |
| `correlationId` | generated | New `X-Correlation-ID` for every request (collection pre-request script) |

Every request body is fully filled in with example customer data, so it can be sent or copied as is. Request IDs
are fixed per test (`QA-PROF-001` for string IDs, `1500010` style for numeric IDs).

## Conventions

* **Test IDs** - `NAME-`, `EMAIL-`, `PHONE-`, `ADDR-`, `PROF-`, `REF-`, `SEC-`, `HLT-` followed by a number. Each
  request's description lists its priority (P1 = critical path, P2 = standard, P3 = edge case), type and expected
  result.
* **Traceability** - every request sends a unique `X-Correlation-ID` (`qa-<uuid>`). For `/validate-profile` this id
  is written to the `validation_audit` table, so a failing run can be traced in the database with
  `SELECT * FROM validation_audit WHERE correlation_id = '<id>'`.
* **Global checks** - every response is checked for: response time under `slaMs`, no 5xx, JSON content type.
* **Example customers** - Michael Thompson (TMW, Katy TX) is the default customer. Other cases use Sarah Johnson
  (JAB online), David Martinez (K&G call centre, Chicago), Emily Chen, Aisha Brown (Dallas), Liam O'Connor
  (Moores, Toronto) and Oliver Smith (UK online).
* **Reference data** - denylist and store-master rules depend on database content and live in folder 06 only. Its
  bodies use the values in `local-seed.sql`. All other folders use example data that should not hit any denylist
  or store row.

## Known gaps found while building this suite

* **Stack traces in error pages** - `server.error.include-stacktrace: always` in the dev / qa / prod profiles makes
  Spring's default error page return the full Java stack trace for 404, 405 and 415 responses. SEC-002, SEC-003
  and SEC-004 fail until it is set to `never`.
* **Denylisted email still reports `syntaxValid=true`** on `/validate-email` - callers must read `warningCodes`.
* **`/validate-name` has no maximum length** on name fields (profile caps them at 100) - see SEC-008.
* **Suffix casing** - roman numeral suffixes are returned title-cased (`Iii`), and `Ph.D.` is rejected - see
  NAME-009 and NAME-028.
* **`/validate-address` does not infer a missing country**, so US state and ZIP are not checked (profile does
  infer it) - see ADDR-035.

## Running in CI (Newman)

```bash
npm install -g newman newman-reporter-htmlextra
newman run CustomerHub-ValidationServices.postman_collection.json \
  -e environments/ValidationServices-TEST.postman_environment.json \
  --env-var baseUrl=https://<test-host> \
  -r cli,junit,htmlextra \
  --reporter-junit-export results/junit.xml \
  --reporter-htmlextra-export results/report.html
```

item.name: 01 Name Validation
item.description:
`POST /api/v1/data-quality/validate-name`

Validates and normalises a person name. Returns **200** when valid and **422** when a hard rule fails (invalid characters, store / business name, unknown title or suffix). Single-character names are a warning only. Missing required fields return **400**.

`requestId` must be a JSON number; `userId` is optional.
